def resize(path, width):
    """Resize an image to the given width, keeping its aspect ratio.

    Args:
        path (str): Path to the input image file.
        width (int): Target width in pixels. Must be positive.

    Returns:
        PIL.Image.Image: The resized image. The height is computed
        from the original aspect ratio.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``width`` is not a positive integer.

    Examples:
        >>> resize("examples/clock.png", 200).size
        (200, 100)
    """
    raise NotImplementedError

docs.title: 만들고 싶은 프로그램(What we want to build)
docs.text: We will build a Python data processing program that takes an Excel spreadsheet of uncategorized bank transactions. It will automatically classifies each transaction using keyword matching. Then it will saves a new Excel file with a populated "Category" column.

docs.title: 사용자 정의 및 해결할 문제(Users and problem)
docs.text: Small business owners, accountants, and personal finance managers manually review and categorize hundreds of bank transactions every month. This program automates that repetitive task to save time and reduce manual entry errors.

docs.title: 입력(Input)
docs.text: The user provides an Excel file containing a month's worth of raw bank transactions stored on their computer. The input file must contain at least Date, Description, and Amount columns.

docs.title: 처리(Processing)
docs.text:
1. Read the input Excel file into a pandas DataFrame.
  2. Analyze the Description field against predefined keyword rules.
  3. Assign matching category names or tag as "Uncategorized" if no match is found.
  4. Append a new "Category" column to the dataset.
  5. Export the dataset as a new Excel file.

docs.title: 결과(Output)
docs.text: The program saves a new Excel file with all original data columns preserved plus a newly populated "Category" column. The original input file remains unchanged.

docs.title: 개발 범위(Scope)
docs.text: Features to include (in scope): - Reading and writing multi-row Excel (.xlsx) files (using pandas and openpyxl) - Core keyword-matching based automatic category classification system - Add a "Category" Column and Export Results to an Excel File - Handling exceptions for unclassified items (assigning the "Uncategorized" tag) - Constructing an Excel dataset of mock transaction records for test validation Features to exclude (out of scope): - Probabilistic reasoning based on machine learning/deep learning - Implementation of a Web Interface (Web UI) or Graphical User Interface (GUI) - Real-time Bank API Integration Limitation: (Undetected or ambiguous transactions may remain as "Uncategorized", so the output Excel file must be reviewed and adjusted manually by the user.)

docs.title: 사용 예시(Usage example)
docs.text: A user uploads a sample Excel sheet containing diverse transactions, [sample_bank_statement.xlsx] The system automatically tags budget categories like "Food", "Transport", and "Fixed Costs" and outputs [categorized_bank_statement.xlsx]. The user opens the file to verify that the system accurately tags categories and inspects any remaining uncategorized items.

docs.title: Team rule
docs.text:
1. Pull request size:
  2. one small function(about 100 changed lines)
  3. Review process:
  4. Reviewer: Everyone aside from author(minimum 2 people)
  5. Time limit: within 48 hours after PR
  6. what blocks a merge: > At least 1 "Request Change" from reviewer > Unresolved conversations in the PR comments
  7. Merge:
  8. Who presses the button: Team leader
  9. Merge Option: Merge Commit (Default)
  10. Post-Merge Action: Delete the branch immediately after a successful merge
  11. Conventions & Communication:
  12. Branch Naming: feature/feature-name (e.g., feature/login, feature/ai-integration)
  13. Commit Message Format: Conventional Commits style feat: ... (adding a feature or functionality) fix: ... (Fixing a bug or error) docs: ... (Updating documentation only) style: ... (Formatting, missing semicolons, or code style changes (no logic change)) refactor: ... (Restructuring code without adding a feature or fixing a bug) test: ... (Adding or updating tests) chore: ... (Maintenance tasks, dependency upgrades, or build config updates)
  14. AI usage: Use the disclosure rule from this course
